# Commands the guard must let through, one per line (blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored).
# They run from a working folder that does not exist, with the test config from helpers.py: protected_dirs lake-data and
# ~/vault-data, protected Supabase project abcdefghijklmnopqrst. Heredoc cases live in the test file.

# git: staging and committing by name, and text that only mentions danger
git add src/app.py README.md
git add -p src/app.py
git add -- 'docs/my file.md'
git commit -m 'reset --hard docs'
git commit -m "guard: block git add -A and rm -rf"
git commit --amend --no-edit
git commit -F msg.txt
git status --short
git diff --stat HEAD~1
git log --oneline -20
git push origin feature/login
git push --force-with-lease origin feature/login
git push -u origin HEAD
git pull --rebase
git fetch --all --prune
git checkout -b feature/x
git checkout main
git checkout -- src/app.py
git restore src/app.py
git restore --staged src/app.py
git restore --staged .
git branch -d merged-branch
git branch --list
git stash push -u -m 'backup 2026-01-01'
git stash list
git stash pop
git reset --keep HEAD~1
git reset --soft HEAD~1
git reset HEAD src/app.py
git clean -n
git clean -fdn
git worktree add ../wt feature
git worktree list
git worktree prune --dry-run
git rebase main
git tag v1.0.0
git cherry-pick abc1234
git add -- ':(exclude)package-lock.json' src/app.py
git add src/ README.md
git switch main
git switch -c feature/x
git switch --detach HEAD~1
git update-ref refs/heads/scratch HEAD
git clean -n -d
git push --force-with-lease origin feature/x:feature/x
echo "never run git reset --hard"
printf '%s\n' 'git clean -fdx' >> notes.md
python3 -c "print('git push --force')"
node -e "console.log('lake-data')"
rg -n "git add -A" docs
grep -rn "rm -rf" .

# protected folders: reads, copies out, backups, look-alike names
cat lake-data/manifest.json
head -5 lake-data/x.csv | wc -l
grep -rn foo lake-data/
ls ~/vault-data
sed -n 1,40p lake-data/notes.md
sqlite3 lake-data/x.db 'select 1'
sqlite3 -readonly lake-data/x.db 'select count(*) from t'
sqlite3 lake-data/x.db '.schema'
sqlite3 lake-data/x.db '.backup /tmp/x.bak'
sqlite3 lake-data/backups/h.bak 'insert into t values (1)'
sqlite3 ~/vault-data/x.db 'select 1'
sqlite3 "file:lake-data/h.db?mode=ro" 'select 1'
cp lake-data/x.csv /tmp/x.csv
rsync -a lake-data/ /tmp/copy/
ln -s lake-data/exports ~/lake-exports
echo x > my-lake-data/a.txt
touch lake-data-old/flag
sed -i 's#lake-data#$LAKE#' scripts/config.sh

# SQL that is not destructive, or runs on a disposable database
psql -c 'select * from t'
psql -c 'ALTER TABLE t DROP CONSTRAINT t_pk'
grep -rn 'DROP TABLE' supabase/migrations
echo "TRUNCATE x" > notes.txt
sqlite3 /tmp/scratch.db 'drop table t'
sqlite3 :memory: 'drop table t'
